grade.first_issue: The claim that the two arithmetic progressions can be made arbitrarily close is false when c/c' is rational; for example, progressions with steps 1 and 2 and initial offset 1/2 remain at least 1/2 apart. Thus constancy among positive defect values is not proved as written (Rule C).
grade.summary: The final classification is correct, and the orbit identity, nonnegativity of the defect, bounds, and converse verification are sound. The first false orbit-approximation claim is locally repairable by choosing orbit points with bounded separation and observing that g and h then tend to zero at infinity. More seriously, the mixed zero/positive case is not excluded: continuity at a zero-defect image point only supplies nearby image values, not nearby positive-defect image values. That unsupported compatibility inference replaces the central argument needed to rule out coexistence, so Rule E caps the score at 3.
strengths: Correctly derives f(f(x))=2f(x)-x and hence c(f(x))=c(x).
Correctly obtains f^{(n)}(x)=x+nc(x) and proves c(x)>=0.
Derives useful two-sided bounds for defect differences when the comparison point lies in Im(f).
Correctly verifies every function f(x)=x+c with c>=0.

errors.description: The density/arbitrary-closeness assertion for rationally related positive defect values is false. Bounded rather than vanishing separation is available and would suffice, but that argument is not written.

The proof claims that continuity of f at a zero-defect image point produces positive-defect image points arbitrarily close to it. Continuity gives no such control over defect levels; all nearby image points could have zero defect. Ruling out mixed levels requires a genuine openness/connectedness or equivalent compatibility argument, which is absent.
